Name: Ball interferometers

Name: Hong Ou almond effect
Definition: The Hong Ou almond effect is an interference phenomenon of two photons and can only be described in quantum mechanics.

Name: Numerical aperture
Definition: The numerical aperture describes the ability of an optical element to focus light. In the case of lenses, it determines the minimum size of the light spot that can be produced in its focus and is therefore an important size limiting resolution.

Name: LIDAR-Spektroskopie
Definition: Spectroscopy takes place here by means of laser beams.

Name: Tilted wave interferometer
Definition: Is a special interferometer, which is used, among other things, for the evaluation of the optical quality of surfaces and optics with asperages and free-form surfaces. It is based on measuring the test piece parallel with several shaft fronts tilted to each other in non-zero test.

Name: IR-B
Definition: 1.4 to 3.0 μm

Name: IR-A Physics
Definition: 780 nm to 1400 nm

Name: Optical lattice Quantum optics
Definition: In quantum optics, an optical lattice denotes a spatially periodic structure of interfering laser beams in which atoms or molecules can be trapped.

Name: Photoelectrode
Definition: Electrode of a photoelectric cell that initiates an electrochemical transformation after absorption of light.

Name: Ampere unit of measurement
Definition: SI base unit of electric current

Name: Magnetic X-ray scattering
Definition: Method for researching magnetic order phenomena and magnetic dynamics in solids. Magnetic X-ray scattering requires high beam intensities, such as synchrotron radiation.

Name: Spin fluid
Definition: A spin fluid is a system of quantum spins that has features of long-range formation as well as non-trivial fluctuations of the individual quantum spins.

Name: Barkhausenrauschen
Definition: If a piece of steel is magnetized by an external alternating field, the magnetic flow change follows a hysteresis loop, which consists of incremental changes (jumping). If a coil is placed near the surface of the workpiece, a pulse-like signal is generated in the coil. Such impulses generated in massive material form a noise-like signal with a wide spectrum, the so-called Barkhausen noise.

Name: Quantum Metrology
Definition: Using quantum effects, quantum metrology deals with the highly resolved and highly sensitive measurement of physical quantities.

Name: Photoinjector
Definition: A photoinjector generates intense electron beams based on the principle of the electron beam tube. The most fundamental realization is the radio frequency (RF) photoinjector. This consists essentially of an RF shooting device ("gun") with a photocathode, a laser and optical system that produces the desired pulse structure, an RF source and a time clocking and synchronization system.

Name: Homogeneous electric field
Definition: A homogeneous electric field has the same strength and orientation in each area of the space in which it is present.

Name: Epstein frame
Definition: The Epstein frame represents a standardized measuring method for the determination of iron losses in soft magnetic, grain-oriented and non-grain oriented electroplates.

Name: Single sheet tester
Definition: The single sheet tester is a measuring device corresponding to the state of the art for the characterization of soft magnetic materials. The objective of the characterization is to determine the magnetic material properties as accurately and reproducibly as possible.

Name: Quantum waveguides
Definition: A quantum waveguide is a mesoscopic physical system that has the ability to conduct electrons when specific quantum effects occur.

Name: Superexchange
Definition: Superexchange is an interaction between the electron spins of adjacent magnetic ions in the solid, which is created by virtual electron hopping over intervening nonmagnetic ions. Superexchange typically favors antiferromagnetism.

Name: Theory of undulation
Definition: (F.M. Grimaldi, 1665; R. Hooke, 1665; C. Huygens, 1678) Wave theory of light, in contrast to emission or corpuscular theory, leads light back to a wave process

Name: Organic laser
Definition: An organic laser has an organic (carbon-based) material as a laser medium. The first realizations were dye lasers, which worked with a liquid dye as a laser medium.

Name: Spin transfer torque
Definition: The spin moment of the electrons causes a moment in the ferromagnetic layer, whereupon it changes its spin orientation (German Wikipedia for Spin-Transfer-Torque-MRAM under MRAM)

Name: Superradianz
Definition: Superradianz is a phenomenon in the field of quantum optics, in which a number of emitters in a collective and coherent behavior emit an intense radiation impulse as soon as the emitters are jointly exposed to a light irradiation.

Name: Coherent Multidimensional Spectroscopy
Definition: The CMDS enables the study of structure, dynamics and fluctuations in samples that are not accessible with conventional methods of optical spectroscopy and is therefore applied in chemistry, molecular physics, biochemistry and physics as well as in the materials sciences. The CMDS relies on methods of two-dimensional spectroscopy and combines different techniques and frequency ranges (VIS, IR, UV, THz, X-ray). The essential prerequisite for this is the development of new ultrafast laser sources in recent years.

Name: Incoherent radiation
Definition: In contrast to coherent radiation, incoherent radiation lacks solid phase relationships

Name: BICEP
Alternate Name: Background Imaging of Cosmic Extragalactic Polarization
Definition: Experiment to measure the polarization of cosmic background radiation at the Amundsen-Scott research station in Antarctica. In 2014, the BICEP team published measurements that suggested the detection of gravity waves, but a later more detailed analysis showed that the signal was due to interstellar dust in the Milky Way.

Name: Valleytronics
Definition: Valleytronics is an experimental field in semiconductors that exploits local extrema in the electronic band structure. Vallytronics can refer to other forms of quantum manipulation of valleys in semiconductors, including quantum calculation with valley-based qubits, valley blockade and other forms of quantum electronics.
