Definition: Exchange and trade (in the sense of multiple use) of digital content for use in various areas of the media industry (e.g. print, TV, cinema, web)

Name: Content provider
Definition: Service providers who provide content for a web site. Unlike the service provider who takes care of the technical infrastructure of a web offer.

Name: Weblog
Definition: Online diary in which individual users, interest groups, organisations or companies list information chronologically and regularly update it with the aim of sharing it with other Internet users (RDA AH-007).

Name: HMS production
Definition: Manufacturing taking complex information into account through IT, cooperation and self-organization of individual autonomous production units (Holone)

Name: Cooperative information system
Definition: Several independent systems that together provide the desired performance

Name: Lindström Quantor
Definition: Generalized logical quantors

Name: Oracle Computer Science
Definition: TT of theoretical computer science

Name: Jukebox Data Technology
Definition: Mass storage system that manages multiple disks (e.g. CD-ROMs)

Name: Tertiärspeicher
Definition: External memory, preferably for backup copies.

Name: Specialised portal
Definition: Structured database or comprehensive link collection to search for professional resources on the Internet

Name: Semantic Web
Definition: 1. The Semantic Web is a W3C activity for the computer-readable presentation of information in the World Wide Web in such a way that it can be used by machines not only for presentation purposes, but for automation, integration and reuse across applications. Technologies relevant to the Semantic Web are e.g. description logics, ontologies, metadata, control systems and information extraction. 2. An extension of today's web with metadata for the enhancement of meaning. 3. A concrete implementation of a distributed semantic network in the development process.

Name: Reciprocal information
Definition: Similarity measure, information measure, measure for the interdependence of two variables, correlation measure mainly used in information theory, image processing, etc.

Name: Deep detection
Definition: Procedure for obtaining depth information from two-dim. illustrations of a three-dim. scene

Name: Assistance system
Definition: Components of technical systems that help people interact with these systems by offering suggestions for action and/or performing partial tasks largely independently. Assistance systems stand between assistance systems (product-related application aids) and expert systems (knowledge-based systems that perform problem-solving or decision-making processes).

Name: Information technology support system
Definition: Summary description for assistance systems, assistance system, counselling/decision support systems, tutor systems, etc.

Name: Meta-day
Definition: Information in the header area of an HTML document

Name: Domain grabbing
Definition: The unlawful registration/blocking of a domain exclusively for the purpose of selling

Name: Type-proof language
Definition: Language property, which is essential at source or bytecode level. It says that in well-typed programs no runtime errors can occur in such a way that operations get arguments of a wrong type. Sufficient condition: Correctness (soundness) of the type system.

Name: Owicki-Gries method
Definition: A specific verification method for parallel programmes

Name: Rely guarantee method
Definition: Eine spez. Verifikationsmethode für parallele Programme

Name: Web Services
Definition: 1. Web Services are software components that link programs running on different network computers to one application via the Internet. (FAZ, October 14, 2003) 2. Web Services are not intended for human users, but for software systems that automatically exchange data and/or access functions on remote computers.

Name: Internetdienst
Definition: Summary term for various information, communication and data transmission services based on the TCP/IP protocol family. Examples of standardized Internet services are: WWW, e-mail, news/usenet, FTP, chats, telnet

Name: Image database
Definition: Database containing mainly image data

Name: Electronic programme guide
Definition: Interactive instrument that guides the viewer through the digital TV offering combines the function of the user interface (of the digital receiver) and a ("built-in") television magazine

Name: Mobile Computing
Definition: Data communication of a mobile computer with other mobile or stationary computers using wireless network technologies. Also in the sense of: Access to the Internet with mobile phone/handheld computers or: Working on the go with the help of small (laptops) or smallest (handheld) computers.

Name: Group communication Communication technology
Definition: 1. Summary of several ancillary processes into a process group. 2. Data exchange between a group of computers. 3. Communication (-stechik!) between more than two partners (Lex. Informatik u. Kommunikationstechnik). 4. Main term for Broadcast, Multicast, Gather and Scatter

Name: Mobile programme
Definition: Model for distributed processing. In this model, instead of or in addition to the data, program code is exchanged between computer nodes and removed for execution (Another model are mobile agents)

Name: BMEcat
Definition: XML-based standard for the exchange of multimedia product catalog data

Name: Run-off function
Definition: term from the Dempster-Shafer theory. Serves instead of the probability function for numerical representation of the uncertainty of the truth content of various statements

Name: Hoax
Definition: E-mailed warnings of (alleged) viruses in e-mails.

Name: Join operation
Definition: Operation combining data from one or more tables in a single result table.

Name: Tetrahedral grids
Definition: Unstructured volume grid of tetrahedral cells

Name: Traffic Engineering
Definition: 1. Design, planning and operation of communication networks under quality and performance aspects (TB Telekom.). 2. Influence of (data) traffic of a network by targeted traffic control (Detken, K.-O.)

Name: Data parallelity
Definition: The simultaneous processing of different data elements on parallel computers.

Name: Algorithmic learning theory
Definition: Research area between AI and Theor. Informatics. in which the learning behavior of algorithms is defined and theoretically investigated (in contrast to empirically oriented machine learning). The most important models are PAC learning, online learning, learning from questions.

Name: Administration
Definition: The task of the service administration is to ensure the contractual quality of the service provided by the service agreement (= individually contractually agreed form of service between service provider and customer).

Name: Volume rendering
Definition: 1. Specific method for volume visualization, where two-D images are directly generated without geometric intermediate representation (e.g. triangle lists). 2. A direct technique for visualizing volume primitives without any intermediate conversion of the volumetric dataset to surface representation.

Name: Abstract syntax tree
Definition: A tree-like representation of programs

Name: Byte code
Definition: A coding of a computer program that the compiler generates during the processing of the source code.

Name: Software platform
Definition: Software layer that provides the functionality to the applications that is required for specific applications

Name: Culling Computer Graphics
Definition: term from computer graphics/virtual reality: Currently invisible areas of the 3D model are eliminated from the visualization process (Lex. Geoinformatics)

Name: Verdeckungsrechnung
Definition: Suppression of those parts of a computer graphics that are concealed with given viewer location (=invisible)

Name: Sichtbarkeitsverfahren
Definition: In computer graphics procedures that decide/calculate whether a graphical element is displayed or not

Name: Graphic hardware
Definition: Summary term for all devices of graphic data processing/computer graphics

Name: Ant algorithm
Definition: Natural anatomical optimization methods that use solution strategies that ants use, for example, in forage search

Name: ACID properties
Definition: The ACID-E. describe the conditions that must be fulfilled in parallel.

Name: Isolation of computer science
Definition: Transactions carried out incidentally shall not affect each other

Name: Atomarity Computer science
Definition: A transaction is complete or not executed at all

Name: Serialisability
Definition: Feature of parallel transactions

Name: Transaction management
Definition: The central control of transactions

Name: Forming of traffic
Definition: Method of control of communication (in networks)

Name: Network Graphical representation
Definition: A diagram for the graphic representation of complex structures, e.g. net plan, Petri net, etc.

Name: Nebenläufigkeitskontrolle
Definition: The goal of the N. is to keep shared data stocks consistent. For this purpose, writing accesses are coordinated by multiple users to one and the same data object.

Name: Algorithmic group theory
Definition: The problem of the A.G. is to solve fundamental problems of group theory by algorithms. (The implementation in software falls into the field of computer algebra)

Name: Relevance feedback
Definition: Method of improving retrieval results based on the user's opinion of relevance

Name: Vector space model
Definition: Information units (documents) and requests (query) are considered vectors in a space stretched by descriptors. The similarity of the vectors is a measure of the similarity of the documents or requests.

Name: Quantum Informatics
Definition: Subject area of information processing and data transmission based on quantum theory

Name: Front-end software
Definition: Software that provides an interface to another program "behind" it, which may not be as user-friendly (FOLDOC).

Name: Graph drawing
Definition: The field of computer science (computer graphics) is concerned with the visualization of graphs, which occur frequently, e.g. in schematics or diagrams. The aim is to arrange nodes, edges and partial graphs as clearly as possible.

Name: Intrusion detection
Alternate Name: Detection of penetration tests, computer science
Definition: Part of the IT security area. Methods and (software) systems with which attacks on computer systems can be detected.

Name: Suffix array
Definition: A full-text index data structure for text search

Name: Collage grammar
Definition: Method for rule-based image generation (computer graphics). A set of hyper-edge substitution rules, an alphabet and an initial collage form a system called collagen grammar.

Name: Unified Software Development Process
Definition: Approach to system development

Name: Object Process Model
Definition: object-oriented data model, object-oriented modeling

Name: Custom Computing Machine
Definition: A computer, where the hardware is optimized to speed up specific applications

Name: Model generation Artificial intelligence
Definition: Methods of automatic proof showing the feasibility of a logical specification by calculating models of specification (Karsten Konrad).

Name: Security protocol
Definition: Recording of all security-related actions in a computer network

Name: CMMI
Definition: Procedure model for the development of software, systems or the integrated development of processes and products. Successor of the model CMM

Name: Star-free language
Definition: Subclass of the regular languages defined by formulas of the 1-th level logic

Name: Prohibited model
Definition: Term from the theory Formal Languages, Automats, Circuits, Complexity, Logic and Algebra

Name: Avatar Computer Science
Definition: Animated representation in virtual worlds

Name: RTP
Definition: Internet protocol for the real-time transmission of audio and video data, which works with unicasting and multicasting services

Name: Mail Server
Definition: A server (program and computer) that stores, manages and distributes emails.

Name: Time-consuming machine
Definition: A finite automatic machine with clock variables and time restrictions

Name: RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT RT
Definition: Efficient protocol for real-time transmission of multimedia data streams over IP networks

Name: Advanced reality Computer science
Definition: Superposition of virtual objects over a real scene

Name: SPQR tree
Definition: SPQR trees represent the disintegration of a two-related graph into three related compenents. They are used to list all embeddings of a graph (author)

Name: Failure-resistant system
Definition: A safety-critical system is "fail-safe" if it remains in a safe state or passes to a safe state ("safe") when certain damage occurs ("fail").

Name: Login
Definition: Logging a user into a computer system. Entering username and password. Also the name for the user ID itself.

Name: Single Sign-On
Definition: SSO gives the user of a (computer) system the possibility to access all systems, applications and resources approved for him with only one login, e.g. by entering a single username and password.

Name: Mensch-Maschine-Schnittstelle
Definition: The means of communication between a human user and a computer.

Name: Image-based rendering
Definition: Unlike geometry-based computer graphics, the IBR uses 2D image data as the starting material for creating new views of a scene.

Name: Plenoptic function
Definition: The pl. function describes the information visually available to a (human) observer at any place and at any time.

Name: Particle system
Definition: Physical model for modelling, simulation or animation of natural phenomena such as grass, fire, plants or forest.

Name: Cookie Internet
Definition: In the Internet environment a smaller file is stored locally on the computer of the surfing person

Name: Text Mining
Definition: The field of T.M. covers a wide range of methods for extracting information from natural language texts. The methods come from the fields of knowledge representation, masch. learning, computer linguistics, information extraction, information retrieval, pattern recognition.

Name: Fuzzy Rule System
Definition: A set of fuzzy rules that are evaluated by a conclusion mechanism.

Name: Socket
Definition: Endpoints for communication connections

Name: Multi-tier architecture
Definition: Client/Server. Architectures is based on a structure into individual software layers (animal=layer). The software components are distributed to several computers.

Name: Inverted list
Definition: List index by inverting texts / documents to search for text in document collections according to certain terms, etc.

Name: Nichtflüchtiger Speicher
Definition: Storage system that does not lose data even when power is switched off.

Name: Reset transaction
Definition: Undoing the change caused by a transaction

Name: Proxy Server
Definition: Deputy server on the Internet

Name: DiffServ
Definition: Service quality mechanism for handling traffic flows in one or more networks

Name: MDA Approach model
Definition: MDA refers to an approach to the development of IT solutions based on a clear separation of functionality and technology.

Name: Scenegraph
Definition: 1. The description of a virtual world in a VRML file. 2. A directed, acyclic graph contains a complete description of a virtual universe, i.e. a complex graphic scene.

Name: Programmcode
Definition: The computer program formulated in a programming language

Name: Zero-Copy
Definition: Utility data is copied directly from the memory of the network hardware into the memory of the application and vice versa. There is neither an intermediate storage in buffers of the operating system nor in such of the communication library.

Name: UB tree
Definition: The UB tree is a specific index structure developed for multidimensional area queries.

Name: Location-related service
Definition: Value added service for mobile phone subscribers providing information tailored to the user's location (local weather forecasts, location-adjusted city maps, location information for emergency calls).

Name: Pre-transmission communication technology
Definition: Transfer of information to mobile devices as long as a good network connection is available in order to have it on the device later when it is needed in a weakly coupled or decoupled operation.

Name: Deadline Schedule
Definition: Special strategy for (processor-)scheduling

Name: Association analysis
Definition: The term association analysis refers to the identification and description of regions or data areas in a database where several values are likely to occur at the same time. The association analysis looks for association rules, with the help of which the results are presented. Since the association rules are identified in the database by algorithms, the association analysis is located in the border area between statistics and computer science. In computer science, this procedure belongs to the field of data mining and KDD (Knowledge Discovery in Databases)

Name: Digital split
Definition: The division of society into those who are able to deal with computers and who speak their language (computer literacy) and those who are not. Digital Divide refers to the growing gap between the different levels of education, income classes and population groups. (Duden - Dictionary of the New Economy)

Name: Contextual system
Definition: A system is context-aware when it is able to extract, interpret and process the context information from its environment and, if necessary, adapt its functionality to the changed environment. Systems/applications that can automatically capture and evaluate the current context of users (place, time, technical/social environment).

Name: Planability analysis
Definition: With the help of the predictability analysis, statements about the temporal properties of a real-time system, which includes more than one real-time process, are made.

Name: Full text
Definition: An electronic resource that provides the entity text of a single work or a bibliographic database that provides the entity text of a significant proportion of the works indexed in it, in addition to the citation and (in most cases) an abstract of each work (ODLIS)

Name: Active document
Definition: Active documents not only consist of passive data containers, but also contain active components. (Shimkat, R.-D.)

Name: Coordination language
Definition: A coordination language is to be understood as a class in which the primitives of language are defined as methods

Name: Datenreplikation
Definition: In the database context, copying a data set

Name: Grid Computing
Definition: Networking of processor resources via the Internet for parallel data processing

Name: NL-complete problem
Definition: Problem that is complete for non-determinist. logarithmic place

Name: Form description
Definition: Computer internal description of the form of an object

Name: Correspondence problem Image processing
Definition: Assignment of corresponding pixels in images. Here, 2 pixels correspond when they are images of the same object point in the real world (scene). Partial problem of image registration.

Name: Freeware
Definition: Software that can be used without any cost. Mostly these are small tools or light versions of shareware programs with limited functionality, which are to make advertising for the paid variant. The programmer usually retains the copyright and the source code for freeware.

Name: Buffer overflow
Definition: A buffer overflow occurs when a program tries to store more data in a memory buffer than there is space in it.

Name: Format string vulnerability
Definition: A format string vulnerability allows a server or attacker to send arbitrary strings to clients and thus crash them. Potentially, an attacker can also inject and execute arbitrary code over the vulnerability.

Name: Softwareschwachstelle
Definition: Vulnerability in a program. Such gaps allow hackers or crackers to access other computers. Programs or instructions that exploit such a gap are called exploit.

Name: Exploit
Definition: 1.A routine, a script, a program or tool that can fully or semi-automatically exploit an existing vulnerability. 2.The demonstration of a vulnerability by an example program. 3.The active "exploring" of a vulnerability.

Name: Visibility Skeleton
Definition: A data structure, a graph used to model visibility information.

Name: URL
Definition: Address for a document (a file) on the Internet. Structure: Protocol type://Network address (to be contacted) Computers/Place of storage

Name: ANSI Z39.50-1995
Definition: US-American. Standard for the definition of application services and the specification of protocols for information retrieval in open communication systems, update of ANSI Z39.50-1992

Name: Large database system
Definition: Large database systems hold large amounts of data (terabyte range), process these very quickly, have fast response times, are transaction-proof in critical areas (Internet)

Name: Legacy system
Definition: Altlast systems. IT jargon for hardware or software systems or components that meet outdated standards, but are still used for compatibility or cost reasons.

Name: Meta-search engine
Definition: A meta search engine is a search engine whose essential feature is that it forwards a search query to several other search engines that collect and process results. This is done by eliminating duplicates, the results are then displayed as in a search engine. (Wikipedia)

Name: Deformable object
Definition: Computer Graphics/Virtual Reality/Visualization/Animation: Objects in virtual environments that can be changed by the influence of other objects (e.g. collision) or by users. Applications: Design of clothes, cartoons, facial expressions, human tissue, surgical simulation and training systems

Name: Active object
Definition: Object in a parallel object-oriented program, which has its own control process (thread) and thus not only reacts to messages, but can independently perform actions and send messages. (Uni Oldenburg FB Informatik)

Name: Retiming
Definition: Repositioning of the registers in a sequential circuit

Name: Wearable computers
Definition: PC that is worn on the body (also integrated in clothes or as glasses or watch) and is currently mainly intended for mobile use in maintenance and service areas

Name: OISC
Definition: Computer with command stock reduced to a command

Name: Publish Subscribe System
Definition: Publish-Subscribe systems are used for the effective distribution of information/messages in a wide variety of applications. Typically, a large number of messages are distributed to interested users via one or more servers. From the large number of published messages, clients can use a subscription to determine what type of information they are interested in. Publish-Subscribe systems are used in numerous applications from Boerseinformation systems to distributed software components.

Name: Notification Service
Definition: For the delivery of a message to all interested consumers, an intermediate instance, the so-called notification service, is responsible. This determines, mostly by means of profiles, the amount of all consumers to which a message is delivered.

Name: Data glove
Definition: Interaction medium with sensor-controlled motion transaction in virtual space and tactile feedback via programmable stimulators

Name: Föderiertes System
Definition: Compilation of co-operating, autonomous, and possibly heterogeneous, component systems (e.g. databases, information, metadata, thesauri).The components are completely independent systems that retain their autonomy within the Federation. However, the system supports a new, integrated view of the distributed or heterogeneous components.

Name: Shear warp procedure
Definition: Method of volume visualization. A hybrid method for perspective projection, which is comparable to parallel projection fast.

Name: Spurmonoid
Definition: Generalization of the Free Monoid. Quantity of all traces with a concatenation operation (sequential composition of process sequences). In computer science usual designation for Free Partial Commutative Monoid.

Name: Track replacement system
Definition: Replacement systems via trace monoids (short: trace replacement systems) generalize both semi-thue systems and vector replacement systems.

Name: Track Informatics
Definition: By Mazurkiewicz 1977 a term introduced into theoretical computer science for the description of incidental processes, which are constructed from atomic actions. Traces can be understood as generalization of words, but can also be described as graph theory or as semi-order. Traces are the elements of a trace monoid.

Name: Ablaufverfolgung
Definition: The gradual monitoring of a programme process

Name: Sicherheitskritisches System
Definition: System/assembly which may lead to the following consequences: loss of life or health, serious damage to the environment, significant loss of system property or destruction, failure to perform important tasks or major economic loss.

Name: Rental server
Definition: A web server rented by the customer from a provider that is exclusively and entirely available to this individual customer. The customer has administrator rights (under Unix/Linux: root rights) and can configure the system according to his own requirements.

Name: Instant Messaging
Definition: Service that allows you to chat in real time or send short messages to other subscribers. Known IM services: AIM, ICQ, Microsoft MSN Messenger, Yahoo! Messenger, Jabber. IM software: Trillian, Miranda. (Wikipedia)

Name: Bounded Model Checking
Definition: Verification technology for circuits, configuration problems or planning problems.

Name: Liveliness Computer science
Definition: property that ensures that certain desired action patterns finally occur in the processes of ancillary and distributed program systems (FernUni Hagen)

Name: Turing test
Definition: Designed by the engl. mathematician Alan Mathison Turing Test for Machine Intelligence

Name: Application Model
Definition: Safety model for loadable code

Name: COTS
Definition: Commercial, cheap, non-specialised standard components (components, products) from the mass market

Name: Information technology report
Definition: 1.The output of data from an application program (B computer). 2.The compilation/presentation of information generated by a specific algorithm from a data base (Business Informatics Lex.).

Name: Octal tree
Definition: Extension of Quadtrees to three dimensions

Name: Digital Rights Management
Definition: 1.Procedure by which the copyright of films, sound recordings or software on electronic data processing systems should be safeguarded and pirated (Wikipedia). 2.Electronic distribution systems for digital content. These enable the secure distribution and exploitation of digital content in the online and offline area (via Internet, CDs, DVDs, mobile playback devices or mobile phones). In addition, they enable efficient rights management and thus open up new business models for digital content (e.g. paid download, subscription of content, pay-per-view). To this end, DRMS uses different protection mechanisms such as encryption, copy protection procedures or digital watermarks (Inst.f. Wirtschaftsinformatik, Uni. Bern)

Name: Konnektor
Definition: Connectors encapsulate the technological breaks between systems. They offer the calling system the functionalities of the called system via an interface. Other tasks are communication, data transformation and error handling. (Internet)

Name: Writing Data processing
Definition: Passing data to a storage or storage medium temporarily or permanently for storage

Name: Burning Data Processing
Definition: 1.The writing of data to an optical storage medium (CD, DVD) with the help of a laser. 2. The writing of programs into a PROM or EPROM

Name: Registration Image processing
Definition: 1.The process of geometric alignment of images or maps, so that objects or cells related to each other match. (Lex. Geoinformatics) 2. The calculation of a transformation that depicts two corresponding image contents in two different coordinate systems.

Name: Transinformation
Definition: Correlation measure of information theory. Mean information content of transmitted information. Statistical mean of information measure.

Name: Texture synthesis
Definition: Production of synthetic digital images of textures that are as close to natural textures as possible

Name: Message Passing
Definition: A method with which parallel processes can communicate with each other (www.netconcept24.de)

Name: Division operation
Definition: Operation of relational algebra, corresponds to the all-quantor in relational calculus. Operations to find data.

Name: Unicasting procedure
Definition: Transfer of information from a transmitter to a receiver (one-to-one).

Name: Refactoring
Definition: By refactoring one improves readability and structure (architecture) of a computer program, but its functionality is preserved (Wikipedia). Refactoring is used intensively in extreme programming.

Name: Concatenation code
Definition: A concatenation code is a finite sequence or link of known codes or series of characters for the construction of new codes

Name: Translation memory
Definition: Database in which a source text is stored in the form of translation units with the corresponding target text (aligned bilingual text collection). This memory as the basis of translation support software offers the translator already existing ("human") translations for reuse. Here, not only identical sentences can be detected, but also similar sentences can be found. (Translation recycling). Translation storage programs are e.g. Trados, Transit, XSDL and Déjà Vu

Name: Mobile database system
Definition: Database system that can manage databases on stationary and mobile computers

Name: IntServ
Definition: Service quality model (sends bandwidth and delay data), see also SW DiffServ

Name: Information quality
Definition: 1.Totality of the requirements for an information (information product) which relate to their suitability for meeting given information requirements.(H.Nohr) 2.Content, meaning and meaning of an information (substantially determined by the environment).(Wikipedia) 3.Information quality is determined by: problem relevance, validity, topicality, conciseness, freedom of objection, verifiability, etc. (F.Riedel)

Name: Virtual Home Environment
Definition: Partial concept of the UMTS standard, which provides the user with its individually configured working environment on different end devices and in different (mobile) networks

Name: Case-modding
Definition: Changing the external appearance of the PC and/or the technical refinement of the hardware components

Name: System Area Network
Definition: Network with high bandwidth and low latency that connects computers within a cluster.

Name: Qualified electronic signature
Definition: The signature law distinguishes between the simple, the advanced and the qualified electronic signature (SigG, §2). The qualified signature enables electronic communication and transaction with full legal force and greatest security and therefore has the same effect as a personal signature after adaptation of the private law laws (e.g. § 126a BGB) in the right-hand traffic.

Name: Collision detection
Definition: 1.Basic technology for many areas of computer graphics (e.g. animation, physical-based simulation, interaction in virtual environments). Their task is to detect contact between virtual objects. 2. Essential component of realistic 3D simulations, automatic collision-free web planning, collision avoidance, etc.

Name: Loading Data processing
Definition: Transferring a program or data from a mass storage to the memory of a computer.

Name: Business Object
Definition: Representation of an object from the real business life. In addition to the type designation and description, the representation includes information about attributes, behavior, relationships and rules. In terms of content, these are technical objects; typical examples of objects represented by business objects are product, invoice, employee etc.

Name: NÖGIS
Definition: System for the collection, storage and presentation of low-energy geogr. information

Name: Progressive coding
Definition: Image encoding in several passes. Thus, an image can be constructed from coarse to fine continuous. Especially used on the web, since the image becomes visible already during the loading process.

Name: Program Slicing
Definition: Procedure for extracting properties of a program

Name: Assum-Guarantee Reasoning
Definition: Verification method for ancillary systems

Name: Integrity Computer Science
Definition: State of a system that does not allow unauthorized modification of its components.

Name: Common source and channel encoding
Definition: By means of a common source and channel encoding, more data or the same amount of data can be transmitted at a lower error rate under the same channel conditions.

Name: Agile Softwareentwicklung
Definition: The concept of different methods of software development, which want to make the development process more effective and more advantageous with lean and flexible "low-tech" approaches and with the greater consideration of human aspects. These approaches are based on the fact that they try to reduce the pure design phase to a minimum and to arrive at executable software in the development process as early as possible, which can then be submitted to the customer at regular short intervals for common coordination. In this way, it should be possible at any time to respond flexibly to customer requests in order to increase customer satisfaction overall. In the meantime, there are a variety of agile methods. Among the most well-known are among others Extreme Programming (XP)

Name: Wiki
Definition: Collectively created and maintained Internet offer, on which basically every user can cooperate (e.g. for online encyclopedias)

Name: Test number
Definition: 1. A number attached to a number during encoding to confirm error-free coding. 2. A number added to an account number or other identification key and recalculated when using the number. This can identify errors that may have occurred when entering the N ummer. (Microsoft-Comp.-Lex.) 3. A one-digit checksum (FOLDOC)

Name: Corner Cutting
Definition: Corner-cutting algorithms allow to refine and smooth curves and surfaces by cutting successive corners of a given polygon.

Name: Adaptive programming
Definition: Extension of object-oriented programming by a class hierarchy encapsulation

Name: Collaboration Computer Science
Definition: Collaborations describe which elements of a system need to communicate in order to perform a certain behavior.

Name: Filter Computer Science
Definition: Programs or parts of programs with which data or files can be changed or selected.

Name: Information filtering
Definition: Reduction of information overload

Name: Inductive logical programming
Definition: 1. ILP combines logical pogramming with machine learning. 2. ILP is an approach to combine inductive learning with predicate logic first stage.

Name: Snake image processing
Definition: The Snake concept is based on the description of the object contour by a parametric curve

Name: Rich Media Content
Definition: Designation for "living content" such as video, audio, flash animations, i.e. everything that goes beyond static texts and images

Name: Storage protection
Definition: The property of operating systems to divide the available memory and separate running programs from each other in such a way that a programming error/crash of a single program does not affect the stability of other programs or the entire system. (Wikipedia)

Name: Keller Informatik
Definition: A basement is a specific data structure (linear list), where the insertion and removal of elements always takes place only at one end.

Name: Overhead communication technology
Definition: Additional data accompanying the actual information to ensure the reliability of the information

Name: Displacement Mapping
Definition: 1. Technique in computer graphics, which is used to give a surface of a three-dimensional object a higher level of detail and thus to achieve a more realistic representation. 2.The generation of geometry data from textures. 3. Procedure to create surface imperfections without having to explicitly model them.

Name: Mapping Computer Graphics
Definition: 1. Applying a texture to an object.(Informatik-HB) 2. Algemien the projection of a bitmap graph on a geometric object. (Computer Graphics Glossary (Internet))

Name: Tesselation
Definition: 1. First step in calculating a 3D image. All objects are divided into polygons (B computers). 2. Subdivision of a 2-D plane or a 3-D volume into discrete, coherent spatial elements that completely cover the plane or volume (GI-Lex.). 3. Discretization of surfaces (Lex.Geography).

Name: Asset Informatics
Definition: Assets are units of concrete content and abstract concepts for knowledge representation in different contexts

Name: PCI Express
Definition: Further development of the PCI bus for higher data transfer rates, also as successor of the AGP standard for graphics cards; standardization by the PCI Special Interest Group

Name: WebDAV
Definition: Extension of the HTTP communication protocol; allows users to jointly edit and manage files on remote web servers; standardization by the IETF

Name: iSCSI
Alternate Name: Internet Small Computer Systems Interface over IP
Internet Small Computer System Interface over IP
Definition: Communication protocol for storage area networks; iSCSI, as standard adopted by the IETF in 2003, connects the SCSI protocol with TCP/IP, thus enabling the cost-effective construction of storage networks based on common Ethernet network components.

Name: Graphic tablet
Definition: A rectangular plastic-coated drawing board (graphic input device), equipped with sensors, which allows to determine and register the exact position of a point or point sequences (lines) by means of a special pin or puck (lupe with integrated crosshairs).

Name: Digitalisierer
Definition: 1. Device that converts analog into digital signals. 2. Graphic input device

Name: Digital certificate
Definition: A digital certificate is a digitally signed certification of safety-critical information by a trustworthy instance.(Z. Nohta)

Name: Popup window
Definition: Browser windows that open in addition to the current main window and lie over the main window. In a popup additional information, e.g. production descriptions or advertising, is displayed.

Name: Live Wire Procedure
Definition: An interactive, semi-automatic, edge-oriented method for image segmentation. In order to segment objects of the image, a characteristic object on the image is roughly outlined by default some points using the mouse, LiveWire then searches between these points for characteristic edges. The problem of edge detection is traced back to the search for an optimal path within a weighted graph.

Name: Warping
Definition: The technique of gradual change of images related to morphing is only used with an initial image, but not with a target image.

Name: Tone mapping
Definition: The final step of a photorealistic image production process (color transformation, sound allocation). Visualization of the lighting solution on output devices.

Name: Just-in-time compiler
Definition: Compiler that translates its bytecode into machine code during the runtime of a Java program.

Name: Disassembler
Definition: Program with which a code in assembler language can be obtained from machine code (counterpart of an assembler)

Name: E-Chalk
Definition: Electronic chalkboard that combines the advantages of the classic chalkboard with the multimedia possibilities

Name: Parametrized complexity
Definition: The essential idea of parametrized complexity is to find a clever splitting of the input into a main part x and a parameter y, so that the runtime is polynomial in x and exponential in y. Thus, the combinatorial explosion is limited to the parameter y. This results in parametrized algorithms having a polynomial runtime for input with fixed parameter.(Uni. Würzburg)

Name: ANSI Z39.50-2003
Definition: US-American. Standard for the definition of application services and the specification of protocols for information retrieval in open communication systems, revision of ANSI Z39.50-1995

Name: Autonomous Computing
Alternate Name: EC internal market, free movement of persons, free movement of persons, freedom to provide services
Definition: Autonomous computing is an approach to achieving self-managed computer systems that require a minimum of human intervention. (IBM)

Name: Semantic caching
Definition: In addition to the data, a description of the data is stored in the cache Advantages: Simplification of the interpretation of information, more efficient processing of queries, etc. (D.v. Verschunder)

Name: Ambient Intelligence
Definition: Massive networking of sensors, radio modules, computer processors to improve everyday life

Name: EPIC architecture
Definition: 1. Further development of VLIW technology, combines it with the advantages of dynamic scheduling. 2. A modern, modified implementation of VLIW architecture is Intel's Itanium CPU, which in this case is called EPIC. (Wikipedia)

Name: Unicode 4.0
Definition: Standard zur Schriftzeichencodierung

Name: Gegenständliche Benutzeroberfläche
Definition: Direct interaction between man and computer with the help of physical objects. These are everyday objects equipped with sensors and/or actuators or specially designed interaction objects, which trigger processes in the superimposed virtual plane through physical manipulation ("grains"). By means of touchable user interface one can manipulate digital information (in the literal sense).

Name: Prefetching
Definition: Access in advance. Premature, speculative fetching or provisioning of data, instructions links etc., e.g. a machine command, while the predecessor is still in work. Increases the processing speed.

Name: Caching
Definition: A procedure to speed up access to a hard drive using a cache.

Name: Sequence Diagram
Definition: An interaction diagram showing the objects involved in a particular interaction and the messages they exchange in a chronological sequence. (http://www.infocopter.com/know-how)

Name: Dynamic statement logic
Definition: A variant of Dynamic Logic that allows only Boolean variables as program variables.

Name: Class Diagram
Definition: A class diagram is used to display the static design view of a system. (http://www.galileocomputing.de/glossary)

Name: Encouraging learning Artificial intelligence
Definition: Learning method (machine learning) which does not explicitly specify an agent (Artificial Intelligence) or an artificial neural network to be trained, but only informs the agent/network after each action whether this action is found to be good or bad.

Name: Penetration test
Definition: The controlled attempt ("joint hacking") to penetrate a particular computer system or network from the outside to identify vulnerabilities. To this end, the same or similar techniques are used, which are also used in a real attack. (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik)

Name: Metamodell
Definition: Models that serve the special purpose of specifying a lot of models.

Name: Ontology Knowledge processing
Definition: 1. An explicit, formal specification of a common conceptualization. 2. A formally defined system of things and/or concepts and relations between these things (Wikipedia). 3. Explicit conceptual formalizations of a field of application (knowledge area, knowledge domain). 4. The representation and formalization of knowledge. 5. Hierarchical order of concepts (W Cognitionswiss.). 6. A set of concepts that are related to each other.

Name: Domino problem
Definition: Problem of theoret. computer science

Name: Captcha
Alternate Name: Completely automated public Turing test to tell computers and human apart
Definition: Fully automatic Turing test to distinguish computers and people

Name: Smoothed Complexity
Definition: Smoothed compatibility is a hybrid of worst-case and average-case complexity

Name: Dijkstra algorithm
Definition: The Dijkstra algorithm finds in one graph the shortest way from one node to another

Name: Wearable Computing
Definition: Research area for the development of portable computer systems (Wearable Computers)

Name: Kryptoanalyse
Definition: 1. Analysis of cryptographic procedures and encrypted messages with the aim to reveal keys or plain text, to identify your own security gaps or to test your own cryptographic procedures. 2. Teaching of attacks on cryptosystems (an attempted cryptoanalysis of third parties is called an attack).

Name: Composite Applications
Definition: Reuse and link the functionality of existing applications

Name: Multimodal system
Definition: 1. Systems that can use several modalities of information transmission (e.g. auditorics, gestures, facial expressions and haptics or language, eye movements, writing, images, etc.) (simultaneously). 2. Systems that use (simultaneous) access via different sensory modalities or communication channels.

Name: Vertex Computer Graphics
Definition: Vertex is in 3D computer graphics a vertex of a primitive

Name: Modellgetriebene Entwicklung
Definition: Model-driven software development deals with the automation of software production. Infrastructure code, subsystems, configurations or entire applications are generated from models. (dpunkt.verlag)

Name: Text technology
Definition: Information enrichment and processing of digitally available texts with standardized award languages. Procedures that are precise and algorithmic and that are applied to texts as semistructured data.

Name: Authoring on the Fly
Definition: A technique with which traditional courses can be brought into a digital form and published on the Internet. Lectures and lectures can thus be followed live on the web, corrected or stored locally on a server for repeated insight. Combination of the areas of lecture recording, teleteaching and production of multimedia teaching documents.

Name: Anycasting procedure
Definition: Addressing type in computer networks

Name: Self-serving routing
Definition: Users send data in a network so that their own packets reach their destination as quickly as possible. (Inst. Theo. Informatik Uni. Lübeck)

Name: Dongle
Definition: Copy protection plugs are used to protect software from unauthorized reproduction. (Wikipedia)

Name: Computer Science Service
Definition: In computer science, the term service generally describes a technical, self-sufficient unit that bundles coherent functionalities to a complex of topics and provides them with a clearly defined interface. (Wikipedia)

Name: Interactive Whiteboard
Definition: Computer-aided, touch-sensitive and interactive projection board

Name: Prozessmuster
Definition: Patterns that include knowledge about activities and processes (processes) in software development

Name: End-to-end principle
Definition: Placement of functions of a network at its ends; design principle for Internet protocols

Name: Boosting
Definition: Reliable and very efficient statistical methods for classification of high-dimensional data (applications: handwriting recognition, searching in the WWW, text categorization, speech recognition). Also used as gradient methods and in machine learning.

Name: Chatbot
Definition: Text-based dialogue systems on the Internet

Name: Artificial society
Definition: Computer programs that embrace the robustness, adaptability and creativity of real social systems (Society for Informatics)

Name: Sozionik
Definition: Interdisciplinary field of research between sociology and artificial intelligence (AI). It is a question of whether and how it is possible to develop computer programs capable of communication and cooperation, which are based on the model of human society. Similar to bionics, biological body functions are used as a model for technical constructions, the task of socionics is to use social processes and structures as an inspiration for the design of distributed computer systems. (Society for Informatics)

Name: Timed system
Definition: Time-controlled systems are characterised by the fact that essential aspects of their behaviour are not controlled by external influences (event-controlled systems) but by a statically defined schedule of operations, whereby this schedule is processed according to a strict time-scale. (TTTech Computertechnik)

Name: Vector Data Type
Definition: Composed data types for listing data or a list of numbers. A one-dimensional array.

Name: Mbus
Definition: A lightweight, news-oriented coordination protocol for group communication between application components. (Dirk Kutscher, University of Bremen)

Name: Mini-Robots
Definition: Small robots that can move freely and perform operations independently with the help of their motors, sensors, software, etc.

Name: Media Informatics
Definition: Media Informatics is the science that deals with the theoretical and technical foundations, the processing, the transmission, as well as the presentation of digital media with the means and methods of computer science. (TB Media Informatics)

Name: Web Forum
Definition: Discussion forum on a website

Name: ANSI/NISO Z39.89-2003
Definition: US-American. Standard for the use of ANSI/NISO Z39.50-2003 in library applications

Name: Demo program
Definition: 1. Variety of a program that is limited in its functionality, duration or otherwise. 2. Prototype that illustrates the appearance on the screen and sometimes also the promised capabilities of a program under development. 3. Independent or embedded program that serves to demonstrate the programming and artistic skills of the programmer and at the same time the performance parameters of the platform used and which also serves as a business card of the author.

Name: Recommendation system
Definition: 1.In recommender systems, recommendations, hints and warnings are submitted to a user based on its user characteristics and current context. (software-kompetenz.de) 2. Recommender systems automatically try to generate recommendations by extracting suggestions from the contributions of other users. (Lex. Business Informatics)

Name: Kollaborative Filterung
Definition: Information is filtered according to the behaviour of other users who were previously interested in similar information. (nethics.net)

Name: Phishing
Definition: Attack with the aim to learn personal information such as passwords or PIN numbers of the victim. In doing so, e-mails are sent from apparently well-known companies, which lure the victim to a web site and ask for personal information there. Phishing is a word creation from "password" and "Fishing"

Name: Command Line
Definition: 1.Character string written in a command language and passed to the command interpreter for execution. 2. Line on the screen in which a command can be entered. 3. Written line of a source program.

Name: Rootkit
Definition: Software tools installed on the compromised system after the intrusion into a computer system to hide the intruder's future logins, hide processes, copy data and cut input.

Name: Global lighting
Definition: In 3D computer graphics, the simulation of all possibilities for the spread of light rays in a 3D scene. This fully complies with the laws of geometrical optics and energy conservation and creates a relatively realistic image. (Wikipedia)

Name: Topic map
Definition: Abstract model with SGML or XML-based data format for the formulation of knowledge ontologies

Name: Nanodot-Speicher
Definition: Information storage with point-shaped nanostructures for non-volatile data storage

Name: Electronic health card
Definition: Further development of the health insurance card, contains in addition to administrative and medical data

Name: Webcam
Definition: Video camera that transmits your recording to the Internet

Name: Proactive computing
Definition: In contrast to interactive computing, where users interact directly (one to one) with their computers, proactive computing computer requirements for the user are forecasting and, in some cases, acting in its place.

Name: Computervisualistik
Definition: 1. Designation for the interdisciplinary computer science course, which is currently only offered in Magdeburg and Koblenz. 2. Computer visualists work on image science topics in the overlap area of computer science and image science with computer methods. 3. Collective designation for: image processing, image understanding (computer vision), pattern recognition, computer graphics and information visualization.

Name: Multiprocessor chip
Definition: Multiprocessor system on one chip

Name: Social Engineering Security
Definition: Manipulation of people due to their credulity. Planning and carrying out attacks on information and systems using the "weakness human". Mainly used in the IT field (screwing of passwords)

Name: Channel image processing
Definition: In digital image processing, a technique with which the Farbildinformation of an image can be stored and called for editing.

Name: Personal Area Network
Definition: Wired or wireless ad hoc network (range a few metres) that can build small devices such as PDAs or mobile phones to communicate with each other or with a larger network

Name: DoS attack
Definition: Attack on a host (server) with the aim of making one or more of its services unfit for work, usually by overloading

Name: BSP Computer architecture
Definition: Scalable multiprocessor system with global communication space and effective synchronization of processors

Name: Decentralized data processing
Definition: Form of electronic data processing, in which several computers are connected via computer network, can exchange data and use common resources, however each autonomously perform its own tasks. (B Computer)

Name: Identity management
Definition: A summary description of technologies that support the process of managing, authenticating and assigning rights to digital users (in heterogeneous systems).

Name: Side channel attack
Definition: Cryptoanalytic method, which is theoretically able to break the encryption algorithm of a chip card, a security token or similar systems with the help of information outside the actual data channel (covered channel). Side channels are e.g. the used computing time, the power consumption, electromagnetic radiation, storage requirements, reactions to false input etc. (Wikipedia)

Name: Web application
Definition: Application software that runs on a web server and is used and operated by a user using a web browser (examples: e-mail services, online auction platforms, online banking systems). Web applications can be used in any computer network that allows the operation of web servers (e.g. Internet, Intranet, Extranet). They run independently in the WWW, i.e. the installation on local computers is not necessary.

Name: World Wide Web 2.0
Definition: The "new" web is technically based on the extensive availability of a wide range of broadband internet accesses, which allow users to create and/or edit the content provided on the Internet themselves. Typical examples of this are wikis, weblogs, podcasts as well as image and video sharing portals. The "new" web is no longer a mere collection of web pages, but a platform for a series of new interactive technologies and services on the Internet.

Name: Soziale Software
Definition: Software systems that support human communication, interaction, and collaboration are common to systems that support the development and maintenance of social networks and communities and work largely through self-organization. Popular examples are weblogs, wikis, web forums, contact exchanges and special systems for specific topics such as collecting photos.

Name: Kripke structure
Definition: Kripke structures are a formalism common in the context of model checking to describe system models. (http://www.software-kompetenz.de)

Name: LAN party
Definition: Event where participants connect their computers to a local network (LAN) to play computer games together

Name: Cybernetics-oriented programming
Definition: New theory in software development

Name: Persistent identifier
Definition: Unique, location-independent identifiers for digital objects to ensure permanent access to digital resources at the same time

Name: Mustersprache
Definition: Collection of design patterns in software development

Name: Trusted Computing
Definition: Approach to the security of IT systems

Name: Vascoda
Definition: German Internet portal that allows access to scientific information

Name: Geodata infrastructure
Definition: complex network for the exchange of spatial data in which geodata producers, geoservice providers and geodata users are linked via a physical data network, usually the Internet.

Name: Functional size measurement
Definition: Software size is understood as the size of software functionality or process of measuring functional size according to ISO 14143-1

Name: Software e-Measurement
Definition: Use of web-oriented technologies in software measurement

Name: Humanoid robot
Definition: Robots with a human form

Name: Code of variable length
Definition: Code that displays source symbols in a variable number of bits; e.g.Huffman code

Name: GEO-LEO
Definition: Deutsches Internet-Portal, which makes it possible to access: www.geo-leo.de for scientific information on the subjects of geosciences, mining, geography and thematic maps

Name: The European Library
Definition: Web portal providing access to the collections (books, journals, electronic media), both in digital and non-digital form, the European national libraries; exists since 2005

Name: Paarungsbasierte Kryptografie
Definition: Design of cryptographic systems using predictable pairings

Name: Application-specific processor
Definition: Processor for a specific task or application

Name: ANSI/NISO Z39.88-2004
Definition: US-American. Standard, responsible OCLC

Name: Audiovisualisation
Definition: Calculation of graphics generated on the basis of acoustic data for the visualization of this data

Name: Computer-assisted translation
Definition: Computer-assisted translation means the use of computer programs to support translators. Computer-assisted translation must not be confused with automatic translation (without or only with very limited involvement of human translators).

Name: CBRAM
Definition: New storage technology based on solid state electrolytes

Name: Blu-ray disc
Definition: As high-definition successor of the DVD developed digital, optical storage medium

Name: HD DVD
Definition: DVD written with blue laser with particularly high storage capacity for digitally stored data, especially films in high-resolution formats.

Name: ASURO
Definition: Free in C programmable robot, developed by the Institute of Robotics and Mechatronics in Oberpfaffenhofen

Name: Web Intelligent System
Definition: Scalable Web-based platform with data collection and analysis components via users to create user profiles

Name: Chord communication protocol
Definition: Search protocol for peer-to-peer systems

Name: WebGraph
Definition: WebGraph is a directed graph where the web pages are the nodes and the hyperlinks the edges

Name: Predictive coding
Definition: Coding based primarily on predictions and conjectures

Name: Default
Definition: Default value for system or program parameters

Name: Video portal
Definition: Website that provides videos for streaming (e.g. Youtube, MyVideo, Clipfish)

Name: Cloud Computing
Definition: Cloud computing refers to the provision of IT infrastructure and services such as storage space, computing power or application software from a service provider over the Internet.

Name: High availability
Definition: Ability of a system to ensure full operation in the event of failure of one of its components

Name: Hypercomputation
Definition: Calculation processes that exceed the Turing predictability, the Church-Turing-These (from the template)

Name: Post-quantum cryptography
Definition: Quantum Computer Resistant Crypto Process

Name: Intelligent camera
Definition: Integrated machine vision system

Name: Uneven error protection
Alternate Name: Imbalances in the protection of errors

Name: DDR SDRAM
Alternate Name: Double Data Rate Synchronous Dynamic Random Access Memory

Name: Europeana
Definition: Internet platform with search function in a selection of European digital libraries, museums and archives. Project based on the infrastructure and experience of the European Library; exists since November 2008

Name: Data profiling
Definition: Method for the analysis of data structure, content and quality

Name: Cross-site scripting
Definition: Exploiting a vulnerability of a web application through malicious script code

Name: Document Server
Definition: Digital library for the publication and archiving of electronic publications in a repository. In contrast to a simple publication on a homepage, the operator of the publication server also ensures the long-term archiving and development of the published documents with the help of bibliographic metadata. Document servers are often used for preprints.

Name: Multiphysics
Definition: Simulation of coupled effects

Name: Physical Computing
Definition: Connection of physical systems with software and hardware to an interactive whole

Name: AAL technology
Alternate Name: Age-appropriate assistance systems for a self-determined life

Name: Sonification
Definition: Transposition of data into non-linguistic sound events or audio information

Name: Telnet
Definition: Protocol to register on the Internet

Name: Agent-oriented software engineering
Definition: Software whose structure and functionality is viewed from the perspective of a lot of agents

Name: Design Science Informatics
Definition: Design science is a sub-area of information systems and represents innovative, targeted artifacts (such as mathematical models, software, natural-language descriptions) to solve current and future problems in organization and management

Name: Graphic Library Programming
Definition: Program library that provides basic graphics output functions

Name: Bookmark Internet
Definition: Internet address stored by a browser

Name: Core Concerns
Definition: Realizes the core functionality of a system

Name: Coroutine
Definition: In computer science, coroutines (including coroutines) are a generalization of the concept of a procedure or function. The fundamental difference between coroutines and procedures is that coroutines can interrupt their process and resume later, maintaining their status.

Name: Semantic File Carving
Definition: Semantic File Carving is a form of file carving based on the content analysis of the proposed files.

Name: File Carving
Definition: A process of retrieving and compiling computer files from fragments with exception of metadata

Name: Kontinuierliche Integration
Definition: Process of regular, complete remodeling and testing in software development

Name: CSMA-CA
Alternate Name: Carrier sense multiple access with collision avoidance

Name: Partial reconfiguration
Definition: Function parts in the FPGA can be reconfigured while other function units continue to run undisturbed

Name: Web Designers
Definition: Continuing vocational training according to regulations of the Chambers of Industry and Commerce or Chambers of Crafts or according to internal regulations of the training providers

Name: Web-Designerin
Definition: Weiterbildungsberuf nach Regelungen der Industrie- und Handelskammern bzw. Handwerkskammern oder nach internen Vorschriften der Lehrgangsträger

Name: Telematics
Definition: The term telematics was formed from word components of "telecommunication" and "informatics" and stands for the common, integrative application of both technologies.

Name: Linked Data
Definition: Data in the WWW (ideally freely available), which are uniquely identified by Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), can be accessed directly via HTTP and enable semantic structuring by mutual linking.

Name: Screencast
Definition: Digital film that records and reproduces software functions on the computer screen.

Name: Discovery Service
Definition: Provides own (catalogue) data and external data in a comprehensive central search engine index and makes it available to users as a "one-stop-shop"

Name: World Wide Web 3.0
Definition: According to John Markoff of Web 3.0, based on the term Web 2.0, the concepts of the semantic web are also referred to when the concepts of the Web 2.0 are added.

Name: Net neutrality
Definition: Name for the value-neutral data transfer on the Internet.

Name: Desktop virtualization
Definition: When virtualizing desktop computers, each user works in their own virtual system environment, which basically behaves like a complete local computer. This is limited to providing a terminal server where several users share the resources of a specially configured operating system.

Name: Graph database
Definition: Database that uses graphs to display and store information.

Name: Distributed hash table
Definition: Data structure for P2P systems

Name: Mobile device management
Definition: Centralised management of mobile devices such as smartphones, sub-notebooks, PDAs or tablet computers by one or more administrators using software

Name: Screenshot
Definition: Recording or output (hardcopy, screen extract) of the current screen content or part thereof

Name: Socioinformatics
Definition: Part of computer science that investigates the interaction between social groups and software systems

Name: Concast-Kommunikation
Definition: send multiple transmitters to a common receiver

Name: Upgrade
Definition: Expansion, extension of the functionality of a soft or hardware product

Name: Open Data
Definition: Free availability and usability of data and the movement behind it.

Name: Copy number variation
Definition: Copy number variation is a form of structural variation of the genetic material that generates deviations in the number of copies of a particular DNA section within a genome.

Name: Cyber-physisches System
Definition: Cyber-physical systems are systems in which information and software technology are connected to mechanical components, whereby data transfer and exchange as well as control and control are carried out via an infrastructure such as the Internet in real time.

Name: Production technology
Definition: Production technology includes processes, measures and equipment for the production of new goods.

Name: Machine to Machine
Definition: Automated exchange of information between terminals

Name: Fortgeschrittene elektronische Unterschrift
Definition: The signature law distinguishes between the simple, the advanced and the qualified electronic signature (SigG, §2). The advanced electronic signature is defined in §2 No. 2 signature law.

Name: Differential machine
Definition: Program-controlled calculator, developed in 1822 by Charles Babbage

Name: Chipless RFID
Definition: Technology that allows discrete tag identification without a chip by printing tags directly on the object

Name: Virtual Factory
Definition: Virtual Factory is a merger of legally independent, heterogeneous companies of different competence orientations into a temporary company network. The objective of the Virtual Factory is to solve temporary orders more efficiently. Virtual factories are created ad hoc and use the modern possibilities of communication.

Name: Smart Factory
Definition: Production environment in which production plants and logistics systems largely organize themselves without human intervention.

Name: Tweet
Definition: Message of max. 280 characters sent via Twitter to the followers of the user; contains frequently shortened links

Name: Cyberterrorism
Definition: Terrorism perpetrated by computer systems using Internet technologies

Name: Microrobotics
Definition: Microrobtics includes miniature robots, especially mobile robots, with dimensions less than 1mm. The printout can also be used for robots handling components with dimensions in the micrometer range.

Name: Micro-robots
Definition: Microrobots are miniuartur robots, most mobile robots, with geometric dimensions of less than 1 mm.

Name: Nanorobotics
Definition: Nanorobotics is concerned with the production of machines, robots whose dimensions are in the nanometer range. Nanorobotics is a sub-area of nanotechnology.

Name: DevOps
Definition: DevOps is a suitcase word from 'Software DEVelopment' and 'Information Technology OPerationS'. It describes models and practices for cooperation and communication between software development and operational IT operations and is intended to cover the entire process of development and productive operation.

Name: Pseudonymisierung
Definition: Pseudonymisation of the processing of personal data in such a way that they can no longer be assigned to a specific data subject without the use of separately and protected information.

Name: ω-Sprache
Definition: Quantities of infinite words are called ω-languages

Name: Reconfigurable Computing
Definition: Reconfigurable Computing is a computer architecture that combines the flexibility of software with the high performance of hardware by using very flexible high-speed computing structures.

Name: Roundtrip engineering
Definition: Roundtrip engineering as a synchronization concept is originally a term from the field of software technology and ensures the conformity of designs and their implementation. Roundtrip engineering deals with the system: design, product and the connecting transformation procedures.

Name: Cooperative system
Definition: A cooperative system consists of many actors who pursue common goals through task-related action as well as by means of interaction and coordination mechanisms. For automation systems, such as in automotive electronics, traffic control technology and process technology, their implementation in the form of cooperative systems represents an approach to master the high complexity and decentralized structure as well as to meet the requirements for robustness and fault tolerance.

Name: ORCID
Definition: Non-proprietary, predominantly numerical code for unambiguous identification of scientific authors

Name: Cybernetics second order
Definition: By Heinz von Foerster founded theory of "cybernetics of cybernetics" or observation of second order

Name: Socio-Cyber Physical Systems
Definition: Socio-Cyber Physical Systems are combined systems of socio-technical and cyber-physical systems.

Name: Esoteric programming language
Definition: Programming languages that have not been developed for practical use, but to implement unusual language concepts

Name: Semantic Computing
Definition: "Semantic Computing (SC) is defined as "Computing with (machine processable) Descriptions of Content and Intentions." It brings together those disciplines concerned with connecting the (often vaguely formulated) intentions of humans with computational content that includes, but is not limited to, structured and semi-structured data, multimedia data, text, programs, services and, even, network behavior." (https://www.worldscientific.com/page/ijsc/aims-scope)

Name: Hashgraph
Definition: Data structure, consensus algorithm, (de)centralized platform without server, developed by the company "Swirlds"; alternative system to "Blockchain".

Name: Extract Transform Load
Definition: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) refers to a process in computer science to combine data from multiple data sources with, where applicable, different structures in a target database. This process is carried out in three steps, from which the name ETL derives.

Name: Hashtag
Definition: The hashtag allows tweets to be searched and analysed for specific topics (e.g. frequency of use as a feature of a thematic trend). Other social networks and media on the Internet are also increasingly using hashtags to mark and label information.

Name: OPNsense
Definition: Open source firewall system; based on "FreeBSD" and the previous version "pfSense".

Name: Webentwicklung
Definition: Web development is the software development of web applications, web services or other complex websites.

Name: Social bots
Definition: Social bots are computer programs that generate communicative activities (e.g. likes, text messages), pretending that they originate from a (fictitious) human person.

Name: Symbolic execution
Definition: Procedures for verifying and validating programmes

Name: Network policy
Definition: Policy field around network-cultural, media-political and media-legal issues.

Name: Troll Internet
Definition: Designation of a person who restricts his or her communication on the Internet to contributions aimed at emotional provocation of other interviewees.

Name: Internet phenomenon
Definition: Concept in the form of a link or an image, sound, text or video file, which spreads quickly over the Internet. The most widely used subform is a memes spread over the Internet.

Name: Open Science
Definition: Collective term for e.g. Open Access, Open Data, Open Educational Resources, Open Methodology, Open Peer Review, Open Source etc. The aim is to make science easier for a larger number of people to access

Name: Digitaler Zwilling
Definition: Digital model of a real object or process. If the physical counterpart exists, its current state can be transferred to the digital twin by means of sensors and data exchange.

Name: Upload Filter
Definition: Server-side software that checks files when uploading, rejects, changes or initiates other measures if necessary. Machine data processing is intended to replace a substantive examination by humans.

Name: Speedrun
Definition: Play through a computer game in as short a time as possible.

Name: Human-in-the-loop
Definition: Human-in-the-loop is the integration of human intelligence into AI processes in order to continuously train and validate AI models and thus achieve the best results in the long term.

Name: Knowledge graph
Definition: A knowledge graph is a knowledge base that uses a graphically structured data model or topology to integrate data.

Name: Non-Fungible Tokens

Name: Draw Bench

Name: Radial friction welding

Name: Orbital friction welding

Name: Roll-bond procedure

Name: Point welding adhesives

Name: Welding of heating coils

Name: Adhesives to blind rivets
Definition: Belongs to the hybrid structure processes and represents the combination of the blind rivet with the bonding.

Name: Laser MSG hybrid welding
Definition: Laser-MSG-Hybrid welding is a welding process in which laser beam welding is combined with a metal protection gas welding process (MIG/MAG).

Name: Hybridschweißen
Definition: Hybrid welding combines laser welding with other welding methods.

Name: Welding rivets
Definition: Used for connecting a component of plastic or non-ferrous metal to a component of steel, non-ferrous metal or plastic, and a composite component subsequently produced by riveting and welding. (patent number DE 102010034183 A1)

Name: Slicer knives
Definition: Slicer knives are called circular disc knives for cutting food products.

Name: Wet grinding
Definition: Grinding with the addition of a liquid abrasive.

Name: Engineering asset management
Definition: Is an emerging inter-disciplinary field that combines the technical issues of asset reliability, safety and performance with financial and managerial skills.

Name: Film vaporisation
