Name: Modelleurin
Definition: Skilled worker or (art) craftswoman who designs models

Name: Bin Picking
Definition: Bin-picking is the automated handling of unordered parts in the manufacturing process, e.g. separation from lattice box or box and feeding or loading of the follow-up machine, e.g. by means of industrial robots as feeding devices.

Name: Rubbing rivets
Definition: The friction riveting is a new point joining process, which is based on mechanical connection (form and force lock) as well as on friction welding technology. The joining partners (basic materials) are connected by means of a metallic bolt. Thermoplastic and metallic materials can be used as basic materials in various combinations.

Name: R2R procedure
Definition: In the production of flexible printed electronics, flexible electronic components, printed on a web of flexible plastic or metal foil, are produced cost-effectively and quickly. Other areas of application of the R2R process are in the field of coating and normal printing of substrates. For this purpose, the starting material on a roll is rolled off, processed and finally rolled up again.

Name: Composite forgings
Definition: Composite forging is the form- and material-locking joining of at least two different materials with simultaneous imaging.

Name: Infrarotschweißen
Definition: Welding using infrared technology in plastic connection technology

Name: Hook key
Definition: Tools for tightening and loosening special fasteners, e.g. round/nut nuts or lids

Name: Wrinkles
Definition: The buckling is a tensile pressure forming according to DIN 8584, in which elongated hollow bodies of low wall thickness are extended on a length section by pressure forces applied in the longitudinal axis at their tangential circumference in the form of a convex (expansion) or concave (neck) abdominal shape.

Name: Hot Roll Bonding
Definition: Two sheets are joined by rolling under heat at high pressure.

Name: Semi-throated rivets
Definition: This process is punching rivets with a half hollow cutting rivet.

Name: Tailored tubes
Definition: If tube-shaped components in bodies are joined together by laser welding and placed in a matrice, then filled with liquids and then pressed with several hundred megapascal internal pressure to the shape of the matrice (internal high pressure forming).

Name: Bolzensetzen
Definition: Inserting by means of bolts, which are hit by explosive force, in DIN 8593-3 referred to as bolt inserting

Name: Grinding fire
Definition: Grinding fire is a thermal damage to the material. Grinding fire occurs during grinding of the workpieces.

Name: Net shape forming
Definition: In net shape forming, the component is manufactured close to the end by forming. The final product has the fixed dimensions without machining after processing.

Name: Rapid Tooling
Definition: The term Rapid Tooling (German: schnell Werkzeugbau) describes an area of application of generative or additive manufacturing processes for the production of tools (English tool) or tool components in tool making or mould making, in particular of plastic injection tools.

Name: Zinc phosphateation
Definition: Zinc phosphating according to EN12476 is a chemical surface treatment for steel. On the material surface a zinc phosphate layer of 1 to 3 micrometers is formed. The layer is absorbent and firmly connected to the base metal.

Name: Z-pinning
Definition: Z-Pinning is a compound technology for mostly bonded fiber composites (prepregs) in Z direction. Z-Pins or Z-Fibres support the bonding strength in Z direction. Z-Pins have a similar shape to pins and are made of metal or also made of fiber composite.

Name: Z-Pin
Definition: With the help of Z-pins or Z-fibres, the bonding strength of mostly glued fibre composites (prepregs) is supported in Z direction. Z-pins have a similar shape to pins and are made of metal or also made of fiber composite.

Name: Preforming
Definition: Preforming refers to processes for the production of an end contour-close, dry reinforcement structure, starting with the semi-finished cutting, the draping for the final contour with connection of the individual layers and final cutting with intermediate, possible handling steps for the production of fiber-reinforced components, especially in the liquid impregnation process.

Name: Wet winding process
Definition: During the wet winding process, the carbon fibers are soaked with duroplastic epoxy resin, wound to a core and the resin is cured in the oven.

Name: Friction-based Injection Clinching Joining
Definition: F-ICJ is a riveting process with a rivet made of plastic. At F-ICL, a metallic tool is used to insert friction energy and pressure into the plastic pin and to deform it into a rivet. Targeted recesses in the joining partner absorb the softened plastic so that stable sink rivets are created. The joining partners can be thermoplastic and metallic materials in different combinations.

Name: Flycutting
Definition: Milling is a cutting process in which the tool cutting performs the main cutting movement. The milling tool rotates and lifts a chip with a cutting edge on its forehead surface or on its circumferential surface. If the movement of the cutting edge is on a large radius one speaks of flycutting. If the flycutting tool is radially attached, linear structures, e.g. diffraction grid, can be produced. If the flycutting tool is mounted on the forehead surface, very large surfaces with particularly low roughness (Ra = 2 to 10 nm) can be produced, e.g. mirrors.

Name: Nadler
Alternate Name: Fowls of the species Gallus domesticus, not put up for retail sale
Definition: Historical profession; manufacture and trade of needles of all kinds, later also buttons

Name: Buttonmaker

Name: Wire embroidery
Definition: Technology to produce homogenous heating elements with high temperature resistant yarns.

Name: Trockenschleifen

Name: Direct Energy Deposition

Name: Drawbars

Name: Manual arc welding
Definition: Manual variation of arc welding, which is part of melting welding.

Name: Dietrich Tool
Definition: Hook-like curved tool for opening locks

Name: Wire Deposition

Definition: In these processes, a metal wire is melted in a gas atmosphere or vacuum by means of a laser beam, electron beam or plasma arc and a component layer is generated from it.

Name: Tower clock
Definition: Monumental clocks housed in towers, churches, town halls, and other public buildings, also known as display clocks.

Name: Räderuhr

Name: Vervielfältigungsapparat

Name: Short-term timer

Name: Magnifying glass

Name: Program control clock
Definition: To control a program timed by the clock (e.g. machine control, washing machine, street lighting).

Name: Schaltuhr
Definition: Clock in conjunction with switches that trigger functions by the manufacture of electrical, formerly also mechanical contacts.

Name: Doorbell
Definition: Mechanical signaling device, which is operated on the outside of the front door. The modern name is doorbell and takes into account the electrical function of the signaling device.

Name: Türklingel
Definition: Electrical signaling device, which is operated on the outside of the front door. The outdated name is door bell and takes into account the mechanical function of the signaling device.

Name: Type lever
Definition: Typewriter, in which the type lever is moved to the type roller when a key is hit. A ribbon between paper and type causes the contrasting impression of the letter or character.

Name: Geological compass
Definition: Special compass for measuring strokes and traps of geologous surfaces, vents, faults, etc. with 360° division or 400-gon division, incline meter, dragonfly and visor device. The objects for east (E) and west (W) are swapped.

Name: Clockwork

Name: Pointer typewriter

Name: ATMOS

Name: Trumpet clock

Name: Weight timer

Name: Spring pull watch

Name: Jakobs Staff Nautical Instrument

Name: Frisian watch
Definition: Chair watch from Friesland with pendulum and weights hanging on chains with special links. The F.U. was made in the 18th and 19th century. The metal dials are richly painted with arabesques, figures and mermaids (Seewiefkes) and decorated with tin ornaments. Also indications of the calendar and the moon phases occur. A decorated cloth above the dial can cover the time indication.

Name: Orpheus clock
Definition: Table clock type of renaissance

Name: Stuhluhr
Definition: Watch type of the 17th and 18th centuries, in which a clockwork of four columns, such as a kind of small chair, stands on an e. wall console

Name: Royal Oak Watch

Name: pulpit clock

Name: Clock
Definition: Timepiece according to the principle of uniform burning of combustible materials, which can also smell.

Name: Oil Clock
Definition: In the Middle Ages and into the Baroque period, the oil lamp, whose falling oil level on a scale on the glass oil container indicated how much time had passed since the lamp was lit.

Name: Floating pendulum clock
Definition: A clock that swings back and forth as a pendulum. Its pivot point is below the dial.

Name: Gravity clock
Definition: General name for all watches, which are driven by their own weight or the influence of gravity.

Name: Hanging clock
Definition: A ball-shaped watch with a horizontal dial in the bottom or a numeric wreath that passes by a fixed pointer on the circumference of the ball.

Name: Ball clock
Definition: A mechanical watch in which a ball rolling off on an inclined plane acts as a gear controller.

Name: Sawing clock
Definition: A playful variant of the gravity watch, in which the watch body is driven by its own weight by sliding downwards on a rack.

Name: Anhängeruhr
Definition: Watch worn visibly on a chain around the neck or a châtelaine on the belt.

Name: Bisama apple clock
Definition: The first portable wheel clocks were partially installed in bisamäpfel (bars worn on a chain around the neck or wrist).

Name: Canned clock
Definition: Early form of the portable watch was created following the model of the drum-shaped table clocks.

Name: Imaginative Form Clock
Definition: Upper term for 17th and 18th century clocks whose cases are artistically designed in unusual forms independent of the function as animals, musical instruments, flowers, etc.

Name: Skull clock
Definition: A 16th and 17th century fantasy clock, in which a clockwork is installed in a metal or ivory skull; if the brain shell or mandible is opened, the dial can be viewed.

Name: Blind watch
Definition: A pocket watch with sublime number symbols and powerful hands without glazing above the dial, during which the time of the blind can be felt.

Name: Revolution clock
Definition: Name for pocket watches with decimal division, which was introduced in France in 1792 during the French Revolution as a replacement for the dual division, but did not prevail together with the decimal period and was abolished in 1795.

Name: Pressure clock
Definition: In the middle of the 19th century, the pocket watch, in which the draw spring is stretched by means of a rack on the ironing button or a chain with a knob.

Name: Railway clock
Definition: Oversized service pocket watch with robust metal housing and a high-quality anchoring unit, which used to serve the train guide for precise adherence to the timetable.

Name: Email Clock
Definition: Name for pocket watches, whose metal housing and often also dials are completely covered with enamel painting.

Name: Gold Email Clock
Definition: Goldemail watches are watches with gold cases and enamel covers, often based on models by well-known artists.

Name: Officer's watch
Definition: Technically completed and decorative travel watches of the 18th and early 19th century, mostly with a brass case, percussion and repetition, often also with quarter-hour stroke and alarm clockwork.

Name: Roscope transport
Definition: A large, cheap pocket watch of the late 19th century. These pocket watches had a very simplified wheelwork, in which all unnecessary parts were saved.

Name: Sack watch
Definition: A pocket watch that you always wear in your clothes (while pocket watches can also be worn openly).

Name: Oignon watch
Definition: A frz. bagwatch of the 17th and early 18th century. Originally used as a mocking, derogatory expression for large, plump and particularly thick pocket watches.

Name: Savonette
Definition: Pocket watch with jump cover for protection over the glazed dial, which jumps up at the touch of a button.

Name: Semi-savonette
Definition: A pocket watch with jump lid, in the middle of which there is a circular glazed opening, in order to be able to read the time even when the lid is closed.

Name: Souscription watch
Definition: Showy pocket watches with hour and five minute classification. Around 1800 on special order and against a deposit (souscription) made by Abraham Louis Breguet.

Name: Short-term alarm clocks
Definition: A short-term alarm clock, now colloquially also "egg clock" or signal clock, is a backward-going alarm clock, which gives an acoustic, optical or mechanical signal after a preset period of time - typically up to 120 minutes.

Name: Eieruhr
Definition: An egg clock was originally called an hourglass, which was filled with finely grated egg shells instead of sand grains. Later, the term is used colloquially for a short-term alarm clock.

Name: Radio alarm clocks
Definition: Combination of clock and radio receiver

Name: Main clock
Definition: A main watch is the time standard of a centrally controlled modern watch system.

Name: Monumentaluhr
Definition: Powerful mechanical clocks, which are usually integrated into buildings.

Name: Altar clock
Definition: An altar clock is a clock with an altar-like wooden housing, whose case front with columns and gables, sometimes even with a painted altar leaf, follows the example of baroque altars.

Name: Night lamp clock
Definition: Table clocks of different shape and construction, on which time can also be read in the dark.

Name: Portal clock
Definition: A watch type where two or more columns form a kind of portal and carry the movement installed in the superstructure.

Name: Religious watch
Definition: Simple frz. Pendule with a crowning bow, with which the case looks like a church portal.

Name: Tower clock
Definition: The type of a clock that was modelled on a clock tower of the Renaissance and often had dials with different indications on all four sides.

Name: Vase clock
Definition: A pendule in the form of a vase or urn.

Name: Globus clock
Definition: A spherical pendant or figure clock with representation of the globe, with fixed pointer and moving number band.

Name: Double pendulum watch
Definition: Pendulum clock with two identical pendulums suspended on a common gallows and usually also two works and dials.

Name: Monstrous clock
Definition: Monstrance clock is called a Renaissance watch type of the 17th century, for which clockworks were incorporated into monstrance-shaped table clocks. Monstrance clocks were also called mirror clocks and have a religious-symbolic character.

Name: Mysteries
Definition: A table clock in which it is impossible to see how the hands work with the movement because of the use of mirrors or other deceptive effects.

Name: Book Watch
Definition: In the 16th and 17th century a popular form clock in the form of a book. Under the foldable cover is the dial.

Name: Cartel clock
Definition: Frz. Version of a wall clock, especially popular in Rococo, in the artful, richly decorated and asymmetrical frame housing made of bronco cast.

Name: Dachluhr
Definition: Special shape of an elongated Austrian wall clock with roof finish, mostly with quality works.

Name: Freemasonry watch
Definition: Pocket or wristwatch for members of the Masonic Lodge. These watches are usually triangular and carry on dial and case Masonic symbols (angle measure, circle, hammer, pellet, lot, water scale).

Name: Konsolenuhr
Definition: A console clock is a clock or pendule standing on a wall console.

Name: Wheelchair clock
Definition: A watch that is designed to be practically its own pendulum. The movement body hangs on a spring suspension and a pendulum rod, it swings back and forth relatively slowly and thus creates its own time normal.

Name: Lantern clock
Definition: A prismatic small, mostly open metal clock with weight drive in the form of a lantern and initially designed as a wall clock on a wall console.

Name: Frame clock
Definition: Designation for clocks, which are inserted as a wall clock into a picture frame and thus act as an image themselves. A special form would be the picture clock

Name: Image clock
Definition: From about 1780 it became fashion to install in oil paintings clock, punch and play movements. In the picture a small dial - mostly on a painted tower - indicates the time.

Name: lantern clock
Definition: Type of Viennese wall clock from the time of the Biedermeier in a slim, simple wooden case with glazed front, whose box attachment formally resembles a lantern.

Name: Surrender
Definition: A simple but sophisticated Black Forest clock. At each stroke the whole wheel has to turn, so that one hears at the hour strokes the intense whirring of the wheel.

Name: Ring clock
Definition: A clock housed in a fingerring instead of a coat of arms stone.

Name: Plate clock
Definition: Plate watches belong to the wall clocks and owe their name to the dial that resembles a plate or plate.

Name: Tower clock
Definition: Simple weight clock with alarm clock and hourly stroke, which was hung up in the tower room and gave the towerer the time to stop the tower bell.

Name: Zappler
Definition: Allg. term for clocks and wall clocks with short, oscillating pendulum in front of the dial (front pendulum).

Name: Carpentry
Definition: A spring-driven spindle watch with short front pendulum placed on the table.

Name: Erotic clock
Definition: Usually a pocket watch with a painted erotic representation or an erotic machine, i.e. with movable figures, which is usually hidden in the watch case.

Name: Carriage clock
Definition: This type of travel watch, usually in the form of a large pocket watch, usually stuck in a leather overbody with sound holes and was fastened either in the carriage or on the saddle to serve as a timepiece on the journey.
